OpenAI’s Tibo said all Pro plans have no 5-hour limits and give 10X, 20X or 50X the usage of Plus (Pro 100, Pro 200 and Pro 500, which also gets ultrafast), and asked whether a Pro 50 plan would make sense.

The Pro 50 question is one of today’s most-liked watch-list posts (7,096 likes); the usage breakdown itself has 6,529 likes. Asked Grok Bot to make a video about how the music on a site was made, starting from a clumsy description of Game Boy-style music that transitions between melody variations (945 likes).

i asked grok bot to make a video about how the music in tibo.dog was made! i started by clumsily describing something i wanted (i have 0 experience making music): gameboyish music, seamlessly transitioning between variations of a main melody like another game i had played (genshin)

one prompt i tried that helped me communicate my goal better was telling bot "i lack the vocabulary to describe what i want" and using the /sharpen skill from pstack. then the /in-your-own-words skill helped me confirm whether or not it understood what i was trying to say

i also used this same trick when making this video, so my agent produced a storyboard and animatic before working on the full thing

knowing the right words is very powerful

Reason, a YC coding agent from Reason Machines, works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Bot and Muse on one network so those tools can share context (38 likes).

GROK BOT BUT FOR PEOPLE WHO ACTUALLY NEED TO CODE

the problem: claude code in one terminal, codex in another, cursor open somewhere, and none of them know what the others are doing

what it is: Reason, a coding agent from Reason Machines (YC) that works with all your other agents on one network: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Bot and Muse

how it works: you drop in a task like "the double boost broke in the last build, find out why and fix it" and the teammates split it up. one reproduces the bug, one traces it, one edits the files and adds a test

what else it does: Reasons remember, wake up on a schedule, and run on your own computer or on a cloud one for the long jobs. bring your own key or your subscription

the best part: the engine is free and open source, and you can try the app for free

agents that actually talk to each other, finally

Andrej Karpathy@karpathy· Nov 1
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
hackertube.org

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

GPT-6 Astra solved two audio/video bugs he had been battling for 18 months: dropped frames from an OBS buffering setting that never turned on, and Windows mic popping that needed a specific driver and audio capture setup (312 likes).

Matthew Berman@MatthewBerman
Astra solved two audio/video bugs I've been battling for 18 months!!

Problem 1: dropped frames
> Occasionally in my videos, it would look like the video was dropping frame rate. Turns out, there's a setting in OBS called "buffering" which was set to auto. I thought auto would...ya know...automatically turn it on when needed. Astra read the OBS logs and figured out it never turned on, thus causing my camera input to drop frames as it overloaded OBS's ability to capture them.

Problem 2: mic popping
> Again, very occasionally, we'd hear weird mic popping sounds in my videos. It would only happen on Windows machines. Astra tracked down the problem. It turns out there was a very specific driver I needed installed and I had to have a very specific audio capture setup.

What a time to be alive.

Used Claude Duet from an Uber to gather assets, spin up Claude Code on a Mac mini to edit video in Blender, rent RunPod compute to render, then review the edit back in Duet, going back and forth five times in about 30 minutes (306 likes).

Riley Brown@rileybrown
never been a better time to be a creative.

today while in an uber, i had claude duet use it's vm to gather assets for a video idea i had, i then had duet spin up a claude code session running on my mac mini at home to edit the video using blender for a few visuals. To render the video faster claude code rented compute by the minute on runpod and rendered the blender scenes, then it finished the render on the mac mini, uploaded it to my video version control app and sent me a link on duet where i reviewed the edit. I went back and forth with claude duet 5 times in the matter of 30 minutes until the video was done. Pretty insane process and was just chatting with an agent the whole time.

this is how i storyboard my video ideas. I make ai mockups of the video before i ever film.
